interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis and seminal vesicle invasion, and the absence of lymphovascular invasion following the robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. The surgical grade was ISUP grade group 2. Countervailing factors include positive surgical margins and a higher preoperative PSA of 9.3. The biopsy demonstrated a higher grade (ISUP grade group 3) than the prostatectomy specimen. Nodal status was documented as negative, which is reassuring. The difference between biopsy and prostatectomy findings introduces uncertainty regarding the true extent of disease. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly widens the uncertainty surrounding the trajectory of the disease. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and subsequent changes would be crucial in refining this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 44.16 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 35.33–52.99 months; its coverage has not been validated.
